cards.b: Shape and support; muscle attachment for movement; protection; red blood cell production.
Skull bone (flat) that protects the brain.
Collarbone; holds the shoulder in position and links the scapula to the sternum.
Shoulder blade; flat bone giving attachment for shoulder muscles.
Forearm bones; the radius is on the thumb side.
Kneecap; protects the knee joint at the front.
Ankle bone linking the tibia and fibula to the foot.

cards.f: Long, short and flat bones: examples
cards.b: Long: femur, humerus. Short: carpals, tarsals. Flat: cranium, scapula, ribs, pelvis.
Immovable (fibrous) joint, e.g. between the bones of the cranium.
Cartilaginous joint allowing small movement, e.g. between the vertebrae.
Freely movable joint with a large range but less stability: shoulder and hip.
Moves only in flexion and extension, more stable: elbow, knee, ankle.
Join bone to bone, stabilise the joint and prevent dislocation.
Flexion decreases the angle at a joint; extension increases it.
Plantar flexion: pointing the toes down. Dorsiflexion: pulling the toes up towards the shin.

short.q: Name the bone in the thigh and the bone known as the kneecap, and state one function of each.
short.model: Femur: muscle attachment for running and kicking. Patella: protects the front of the knee joint.

short.q: Explain why the shoulder joint is less stable than the knee joint.
short.model: The shoulder is a ball and socket joint with a shallow socket and a large range of movement, so it is less stable. The knee is a hinge that moves in one direction only.
points: Shoulder is ball and socket with larger range
Larger range means less stable / hinge is more stable

short.q: Name the movement at the elbow and knee when a footballer kicks a ball.
short.model: At the knee: extension as the leg straightens. At the elbow: flexion as the arm bends for balance.
points: Flexion at elbow (or accept suitable alternative)

short.q: Give two ways the skeleton helps a goalkeeper.
short.model: It protects organs such as the brain and the heart when landing, and gives muscles bones to pull on to move quickly.

short.q: Describe the movement of the ankle as a sprinter pushes off the blocks.
short.model: Plantar flexion: the toes point down and the foot extends away from the shin, driven by the gastrocnemius.
points: Toes point down / foot pushes away
